q: What exactly is a tracked query?
a: One prompt a buyer would ask, checked on every engine in your plan, at your plan's refresh rate. 100 queries on Starter means 100 prompts — engines and frequency don't multiply the count.
ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews on every plan; Perplexity and Gemini from Growth; Copilot and Claude on Scale and above. Coverage changes are flagged in the changelog.

q: Where do the queries come from?
a: We propose a set from your site, your Search Console data if connected, and your category. You edit everything — swap, add, or retire queries whenever you like.
The free scan is the trial — a real reading on your real domain, no account. Paid plans start with your scan history intact, so nothing is measured twice.

q: What happens when I hit my limit?
a: Scans keep running. You see a banner, and the overage block ($19 per 100 queries) is billed at the end of the cycle. We never stop measuring mid-month.

q: Why are competitor names locked on Starter?
a: Starter answers "do I have a problem." Naming who benefits is the analysis layer, and it's the honest line between the two plans — not an artificial crippling of the data.

q: Can I cancel or downgrade anytime?
a: Yes, from billing settings, effective at the end of the cycle. Your history is exportable for 90 days after cancellation.

q: How is the citation rate calculated?
a: Cited answer runs divided by total answer runs, per query, per engine. Citations are matched by resolved URL. The method page shows one query end to end.

q: Do competitors know I track them?
a: No. We read public engine answers; we never touch competitor properties. They appear because engines cite them, not because we crawled them.
Card on all self-serve plans, handled by our merchant of record with VAT and sales tax included. Invoicing is available on Enterprise.
Your query set and results are yours; we never train on them or show them to anyone else. DPA and subprocessor list are on the legal pages, signed DPA on Enterprise.
Queries can be in any language the engines answer. Cause attribution currently performs best in English; we say so rather than pretend otherwise.
